candidates.evidence: Direct population studies support both the minority-permissive and majority-opposed orientations without relying on the ASRM opinion. Dahl et al. surveyed 1,197 US adults aged 18-45: 8% would use preconception sex-selection technology, 74% were opposed, and 50% preferred an equal number of boys and girls, connecting the small prospective demand to family-balance preferences (PMID 16595229). Winkelman et al. surveyed a nationally representative US sample of 1,006 adults: 21.1% supported PGD for sex selection, 51.5% disagreed or strongly disagreed, and 27.4% were neutral (PMID 25758988). Kippen, Gray and Evans analyzed the 2007 and 2016 Australian Survey of Social Attitudes; in 2016 roughly three quarters opposed legalizing IVF sex selection for any reason or for family balancing of a second or third child, directly matching the family-balancing policy axis (PMID 30185179). An earlier representative German survey found 11% approved nonmedical preconception sex selection and 32% favored strict prohibition (PMID 15670402). These studies establish genuine public disagreement while showing that the permissive orientation is a minority position, not majority support.
